content.title: About
content.content: Air‑popped popcorn with added butter is a light, crunchy snack. The popcorn is first popped without oil, then a small amount of melted butter is mixed in to give a rich, buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Air‑popped popcorn contains less fat than traditional oil‑popped popcorn.
Butter is added after popping to preserve the crisp texture of the kernels.
Popcorn is one of the most popular cinema snacks worldwide.
The corn used for popcorn is the only variety that ‘pops’ when heated.
Popcorn can be used in salads, desserts, and even as a coating for fried foods.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Air‑popped popcorn without added oil provides about 30 kcal per gram, making it a good option for weight control.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Popcorn is a source of dietary fiber, which supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Corn kernels contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Popcorn is naturally gluten‑free, suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn provides B1, B3 and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If salted butter is used, the sodium level can be high, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Butter may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to milk proteins.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The light texture can lead to rapid consumption of large portions.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Using partially hydrogenated butter can introduce trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popcorn can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to movie‑night mixes, tossed into salads, or sprinkled with spices or cheese. For a richer taste, gently reheat the popcorn with a little extra butter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store popcorn in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep it refrigerated to prevent the butter from going rancid.
